name: Adversarial imitation
positive_test: trains a discriminator to separate agent from expert transitions and uses it as reward
negative_test: matching actions pointwise
examples: GAIL, DAC, AIRL, f-GAIL

name: Instance-discrimination contrastive learning
positive_test: pulls together views of the same instance and explicitly pushes apart other instances
negative_test: a method with no negative examples in its loss
examples: InstDisc, CPC, MoCo, MoCo v2, MoCo v3, SimCLR, SimCLR v2

name: Cross-modal contrastive alignment
positive_test: contrasts paired items from two different modalities against mismatched pairs
negative_test: contrasting two augmented views of one item
examples: CLIP, ALIGN, SigLIP, AudioCLIP, ImageBind
notes: pairing is a supervision source, which blurs self vs supervised

name: Label-aware contrastive learning
positive_test: treats all same-class examples as positives using ground-truth labels
negative_test: treating only augmented views of one instance as positives
examples: SupCon, contrastive representation distillation

name: Negative-free self-distillation
positive_test: regresses a student view onto a target produced by a momentum or stop-gradient copy
negative_test: a loss containing explicit negative pairs
examples: Mean Teacher, BYOL, SimSiam, DINO, DINOv2
notes: collapse avoidance is the defining engineering problem

name: Redundancy-reduction objectives
positive_test: decorrelates embedding dimensions via a cross-correlation or covariance criterion
negative_test: contrasting whole embeddings against other samples
examples: Barlow Twins, VICReg, VICRegL, W-MSE

name: Clustering-based self-supervision
positive_test: alternates assigning pseudo-cluster labels and predicting them from another view
negative_test: a loss defined directly between embeddings with no assignment step
examples: DeepCluster, SeLa, SwAV, PCL, ODC

name: Masked-input prediction
characteristic: what is masked and what the reconstruction target is
positive_test: hides part of the input and trains the model to recover it from the remainder
negative_test: predicting the next element with no masking of a visible context
examples: BERT MLM, MAE, wav2vec 2.0

name: Masked language modelling
positive_test: masks tokens and predicts their identity from bidirectional context
negative_test: predicting only the next token left to right
examples: CBOW, BERT MLM, RoBERTa, SpanBERT, T5 span corruption, ELECTRA
notes: ELECTRA replaces the target with a detection task

name: Masked visual modelling
positive_test: masks image or video patches and reconstructs pixels, tokens or features
negative_test: reconstructing the whole unmasked image
examples: Context Encoders, BEiT, MAE, SimMIM, iBOT, VideoMAE

name: Masked and contrastive speech modelling
positive_test: masks spans of audio and predicts quantised or clustered units
negative_test: predicting transcribed text
examples: wav2vec, wav2vec 2.0, HuBERT, WavLM, data2vec

name: Handcrafted pretext tasks
positive_test: invents a label from a known transformation of the input and predicts it
negative_test: predicting part of the raw input content itself
examples: relative patch position, jigsaw, rotation prediction, colourisation, shuffle-and-learn
notes: largely historical; kept as an aggregation ancestor

name: Latent predictive self-supervision
positive_test: predicts the representation of unobserved content rather than its raw content
negative_test: regressing raw pixels or tokens
examples: CPC, I-JEPA, V-JEPA, SPR, PBL
notes: SPR applies this inside RL, hence multi-parent

name: Shallow embedding induction
characteristic: what co-occurrence structure the embedding factorises
positive_test: fits a lookup-table embedding directly from co-occurrence statistics, with no deep encoder
negative_test: training a deep encoder end to end
examples: word2vec, GloVe, fastText, DeepWalk, node2vec, item2vec
notes: produces a model, but the procedure is the entry

name: Autoregressive density modelling
positive_test: factorises the joint density into a product of conditionals and fits each by maximum likelihood
negative_test: fitting a bound on the likelihood or an implicit density
examples: n-gram MLE, neural LM, PixelRNN, PixelCNN, causal LM pretraining, WaveNet training
notes: the dominant pretraining objective; needs its own ancestor

name: Exposure-bias corrections
positive_test: changes which context the model conditions on during training to match inference
negative_test: plain teacher forcing
examples: scheduled sampling, professor forcing, SeqGAN-style corrections

name: Adversarial generative training
characteristic: which part of the minimax setup is altered
positive_test: trains a generator against a discriminator whose loss it maximises
negative_test: any objective with an explicit likelihood or reconstruction term
examples: GAN, WGAN, StyleGAN, CycleGAN

name: Adversarial divergence variants
positive_test: changes the divergence or the discriminator's loss form
negative_test: changes conditioning or architecture only
examples: LSGAN, WGAN, WGAN-GP, SN-GAN, hinge GAN, f-GAN, relativistic GAN

name: Conditional and translation GANs
positive_test: conditions the generator on a label, image or text and pairs or cycles the mapping
negative_test: unconditional sampling
examples: cGAN, pix2pix, CycleGAN, StarGAN, SPADE

name: Adversarial training stabilisers
positive_test: adds a regulariser or update-timing rule aimed at the minimax dynamics
negative_test: a change in the generator's data distribution
examples: R1 regularisation, instance noise, TTUR, PPL regularisation, ADA

name: Normalizing flows
characteristic: how the invertible map is constructed
positive_test: models density through an exactly invertible map with a tractable Jacobian determinant
negative_test: a non-invertible decoder with a bound
examples: NICE, RealNVP, Glow, MAF, IAF

name: Continuous-time flows
positive_test: defines the map as the solution of a learned ODE rather than a stack of coupling layers
negative_test: discrete stacked bijectors
examples: Neural ODE, FFJORD, rectified flow, flow matching, stochastic interpolants
notes: flow matching is also the modern diffusion-training formulation

name: Score-based and diffusion modelling
positive_test: learns the score or the noise of a progressively corrupted data distribution
negative_test: learning an exact or bounded likelihood of the clean data directly
examples: score matching, denoising score matching, NCSN, DDPM, improved DDPM, EDM, SDE diffusion

name: Guidance of the diffusion trajectory
positive_test: steers sampling with an external or implicit conditional signal during generation
negative_test: conditioning only through the training objective
examples: classifier guidance, classifier-free guidance, ControlNet conditioning, CFG rescaling
notes: role is decoding although the lineage is generative

name: Latent-space diffusion
positive_test: runs the diffusion process in a learned compressed space rather than pixel space
negative_test: diffusing directly on raw observations
examples: latent diffusion, Stable Diffusion training, DiT training

name: Diffusion samplers and distillation
positive_test: reduces the number of denoising steps needed to produce a sample
negative_test: the training procedure that fits the denoiser
examples: DDIM, DPM-Solver, UniPC, progressive distillation, consistency models, LCM
notes: lineage drifts from objective to decoder; see Tensions

name: Energy-based modelling
positive_test: fits an unnormalised energy whose normaliser is never computed exactly
negative_test: a model with a tractable normalising constant
examples: Boltzmann machine, RBM, contrastive divergence, deep belief net, JEM, Langevin EBM

name: Multi-objective gradient surgery
positive_test: alters per-task gradients to remove mutual interference before summing
negative_test: weighting task losses as scalars
examples: PCGrad, CAGrad, GradDrop, GradNorm

name: Adversarial domain alignment
positive_test: trains a domain discriminator the feature extractor is trained to fool
negative_test: matching moments or kernels in closed form
examples: DANN, ADDA, CDAN, MDD

name: Multi-task and auxiliary objectives
positive_test: fits one parameter set against two or more distinct task losses
negative_test: finetuning sequentially, one task at a time
examples: uniform weighting, uncertainty weighting, GradNorm, UNREAL auxiliary tasks

name: Learned dense retrieval
positive_test: scores by inner product of learned query and document embeddings
negative_test: scoring by term statistics
examples: DSSM, DPR, ANCE, ColBERT, E5, GTE
notes: trained contrastively, used at inference

name: Self-supervised test-time training
positive_test: takes gradient steps on an auxiliary self-supervised loss computed on the test input
negative_test: using the task head's own entropy
examples: TTT, TTT-MAE, MEMO, TTT-layers
